title: Build Night: Demos, Collabs & Open Source in Practice
description:
A fortnightly, hands-on session focused on the projects the Auckland AI Collective is actually building — together.

Each session centres on **demonstrations** of what members are working on. Expect live demos, group experiments, and the occasional "let's just try it and see what happens" moment — so come ready to get involved, not just watch. Some parts may invite your participation; none of it is polished or precious.

The tone is **casual and informal**\- eat dinner\, drink\, and enjoy\. This is a place to share ideas\, get feedback\, find collaborators\, and turn "someone should build that" into an actual repo\.

What we cover will vary week to week depending on what people bring and what the group is curious about — the constant is the room: builders comparing notes and starting things together.

**This is for you if** you want to get directly and personally involved in group projects, collaborations, and **open source**.

See what we're already building on GitHub: [https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective](https://github.com/auckland-ai-collective)

Bring a project, a problem, an idea, or just yourself.

After this session we can hang out as long as we like at the restaurant if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

title: Welcome to the next AWS Auckland Well-Architected Meetup for 2026!
location: Level 13, Commercial Bay, 15 Customs Street West, Auckland CBD, Auckland 1010, Auckland
description:
Hi Architects,

Welcome to the next AWS Auckland Well Architected User Group Meetup of 2026!

At each meetup, we focus on learning and networking in a friendly and inclusive atmosphere and explore best-practices in AWS. This has resulted in the AWS Well-Architected Meetups becoming the most popular AWS Meetups in ANZ 🥳

**Please also note that AWS Security now requests a company name and company email where it is available. If you are a student, please list your institution and your student email address at that institution 👍**

We'll be announcing more speakers on [https://well-architected.me](https://well-architected.me/) and previewing presentations during the coming weeks - our speakers and details this month include:

* **Michael Taylor, Lakebase Specialist, Databricks**

**How Lakebase provides a well-architected platform for next generation application and AI development.**
Come and hear how Databricks experts show how customers run applications and agents on Lakebase; serverless Postgres governed by Unity Catalog. See instant branching, scale-to-zero, point-in-time recovery and synced tables in action. The Databricks team will also give a first look at LTAP; one open, governed copy of data for transactions and analytics, with no ETL in between.

* **Kristof Ringleff, Solution Architect, Fooman**

**From Weekend Project to Well-Architected: Putting AWS's new Well-Architected Agent to Work**

Kristoff had a small serverless weekend project running on AWS. So he pointed the brand-new AWS Well-Architected Agent at it. Then I did what any sensible engineer would do with a hobby app; I followed its advice. This talk covers what the agent found, what I learned along the way and the fun of over-engineering something that never needed it. I'll also compare it with the open-source Well-Architected Review skill, which runs in your own coding agent and needs no AWS Support plan.

* **Mystery Speaker**

**The AWS AI Competency - can automation support?**

title: OWASP New Zealand - Auckland Meetup

description:
Join us for the next **OWASP New Zealand Chapter** meetup! We are gathering the local application security community for an evening of technical talks, networking, and knowledge sharing.

* **When:** Tuesday, 10th November 2026
* **Where:** **ASB North Wharf**, 'The Cube', ASB North Wharf, 12 Jellicoe Street 1010, New Zealand
* **Time:** 5:30 PM (Doors open for networking), 6:00 PM (Presentations begin)

We present an introductory talk about the OWASP Top 10 (2025 edition) with a new item each meeting. In the current storm of PHP2Shell, Brotli/HTTP2Shell/Node2Shell, and eMudhra, we'll be covering something very topical - A03:2025 Software Supply Chain Failures.

**Thanks to Our Host**
A big thank you to ASB for sponsoring the venue and for supporting the local security community.

**Agenda**

* 6:00 PM OWASP Introduction, Top 10
* 6:30 PM Break
* 6:45 PM Technical Talk

**Technical Topic Speaker: Michael Matthee, CyberCX/Accenture**
**Talk Title: Secure Vibe Coding**
Following on from OWASP NZ Day 2026, Michael will run his popular Secure Vibe Coding Workshop! In this workshop, you’ll use AI to vibe-code a small feature together with the instructor and group, allow a few realistic AI-generated mistakes to slip through, and then prevent those issues using better specifications, guardrails, secure principles and practices in AI-assisted software engineering.
\-\-\-\-
OWASP Auckland is on Meetup for now - please watch this space.

We're always looking for presenters and topics for future meetings - contact Austin (austin.chamberlain@appsec.org.nz) if you have an idea for a topic, or a presentation you'd like to make. That way, it won't always be Austin talking about what he's been working on recently.

The Auckland-area OWASP Meetup usually takes place on the third Tuesdays of March, May, July, September, and November. There is no Meetup in January, as our members enjoy their holidays.

title: JuniorDev Auckland Meet
location: 125 The Strand, Parnell, Auckland 1010, New Zealand, Auckland
description:
We’re happy to announce the next **JuniorDev Auckland event**!

Join us for an evening of learning and connection as we hear from our speakers and the experiences they’ll be sharing.

**Important Note for Attendees:**

* **Please note of the new location for the event: [Directions to Serko House](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1M8Jt_-5DmBABSiNnaDpCpNiHNfxMRCICI1eRBjne-08/edit?tab=t.0) (Just 2 mins away from Xero)**

**Talk 1: Finding Joy After AI: An Inside Out Look at How We Work by Kevin Meneses**
Inspired by Disney and Pixar's Inside Out films, this (pre-recorded) talk uses their premise as a framework to explore what team survey data reveals about AI adoption, productivity, and working hours, offering practical ways to thrive in an AI-assisted workflow.

**A bit about Kevin:**

* Kevin is a Junior Software Engineer at Fergus who transitioned into engineering from the Customer Support team after completing a full stack developer programme.

**Talk 2: Building AI without Losing Our Values by**
**Lauren Peate**
AI is here to stay – hype, copyright theft, data worker mistreatment, environmental harm, and all. If you care about people and the planet but also need to understand new tech, what can you do? I’ll recommend a middle ground – using AI in features and workflows without compromising our values. Combining my own experience with insights from our original research with hundreds of global developers, I’ll share examples of how to use this tech with care.

**A bit about Lauren:**

* Lauren Peate is a data nerd who cares about people. She’s founder and CEO of Multitudes, which turns engineering metrics into a tool for continuous improvement – in AI, engineering productivity, developer experience, and more. Through her career, she’s worked with a wide range of organizations, from Fortune 500 tech companies in San Francisco to startups in the Middle East. Previously on a PhD track, she started her career conducting independent research through a Fulbright grant.

title: Prompt, Cast, Render: AI Video Production Start to Finish
description:
AI video demos look effortless. Finished work isn’t. A thirty-second spot still needs a plan, a product that looks like itself in every frame, sound, and an edit, and the tools change every month.

This is a demo and discussion session on how AI video actually gets made, from the first prompt to the final export. We’ll generate on screen, walk through the workflows behind finished pieces, and talk about what’s worth using today. Bring the tools you already use and the shot you can’t get to work.

We’ll explore:

* The state of AI video. What’s production-ready, what’s still a party trick, and what has changed since the last time you looked.
* Generation workflows. Text-to-video, image-to-video and reference-driven approaches, and when each one earns its place.
* Marketing video, start to finish. Concept, script, shots, product accuracy and brand consistency, turned around in an afternoon.
* The production process. Briefs, shot lists, coverage and continuity, and how to keep characters and products consistent across shots.
* Tools and techniques. Models, editors and upscalers, plus prompting for motion, camera and pacing rather than stills.
* Cost and speed. What a finished minute really costs in time and money, and when running models locally makes sense.
* Finishing. Dialogue, sound, colour and the edit, which quietly do most of the heavy lifting.
* Rights and disclosure. Commercial licensing, client work and sensible defaults.
* Knowing when to stop. Where AI footage falls apart, and when it’s better to shoot it for real.

No prior background assumed. If you make video, market a product, commission it for a team, or just want to know what’s possible now, this is for you.
Afterwards we usually continue over dinner nearby, a good chance to connect with fellow builders and practitioners.

title: Peeking Under the Hood of Linux & Android + Open Networking
description:
Looking for a chill but productive space to code, learn, and connect with other developers? Whether you’re just starting out or deep into a side project, you’re welcome here.

🚨 **Special Feature This Week: Peeking Under the Hood of Linux & Android**

This week features a deep dive by [Tao Liu](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tao-liu-151618184), an expert Senior Software Engineer. He will be walking us through the fundamentals of inline hooking and its implementation within Linux kernel programming.

He’ll be breaking down the core concepts and implementation:

* **The Basics:** An introduction to what an inline hook actually is, alongside a foundational overview of the Linux kernel.
* **The Integration:** How inline hooks and the Linux kernel come together, including how to successfully implement them.
* **Use Cases & Live Demo:** A discussion on the practical, real-world applications for this technique, concluding with a live demonstration of inline hooking in action on an Android device.

Alongside the demo, this remains a casual, community-driven space where you can:

* 💻 Work on your own coding projects
* 🎯 Share goals or progress (totally optional!)
* 🎙️ Talk tech, app development, and open networking
* ☕ Meet like-minded people over coffee

Come with your laptop, your curiosity, or just a love for tech. Stay for the connections and good vibes.

☕ This event is hosted at a local café, so we kindly ask that you support the venue by purchasing a drink or snack if you can.

No pressure, no strict schedule—just code, coffee, AI, and vibes.
We usually hold meetups every fortnight (bi-weekly)—use them to connect, share, and learn from others.

For your deep work sessions between meetups, feel free to try NeonContext: a Voice AI tool designed to help you stay focused and hit your flow state.
